---
title: "randomNames()"
subtitle: "Generate random first and last names"
toc: true
---

## Usage

``` R
randomNames(
  n,
  gender,
  ethnicity,
  which.names = "both",
  name.order = "last.first",
  name.sep = ", ",
  sample.with.replacement = TRUE,
  return.complete.data = FALSE
)
```

## Arguments

`n`{#n}

:   Optional. A single positive whole number: how many names to produce. Defaults to 1. Most useful when no gender or ethnicity is supplied.

`gender`{#gender}

:   Optional. A vector of genders, either codes (`0` male, `1` female) or text as described in Details.

`ethnicity`{#ethnicity}

:   Optional. A vector of ethnicities, either codes or text as described in Details. The codes are:

    1

    :   American Indian or Native Alaskan

    2

    :   Asian or Pacific Islander

    3

    :   Black (not Hispanic)

    4

    :   Hispanic

    5

    :   White (not Hispanic)

    6

    :   Middle-Eastern, Arabic

`which.names`{#which.names}

:   One of `"both"` (the default), `"first"` or `"last"`.

`name.order`{#name.order}

:   When `which.names` is `"both"`, either `"last.first"` (the default) or `"first.last"`.

`name.sep`{#name.sep}

:   When `which.names` is `"both"`, the string placed between the two names. Defaults to `", "`.

`sample.with.replacement`{#sample.with.replacement}

:   Sample names with replacement? Defaults to `TRUE`. Without replacement the number of names asked for in one gender and ethnicity group cannot exceed the names available for it.

`return.complete.data`{#return.complete.data}

:   Return a `data.table` with the `ethnicity` and `gender` codes used alongside the names, instead of a character vector. Defaults to `FALSE`.

## Value

A character vector of names, or, when `return.complete.data = TRUE`, a `data.table` with columns `gender`, `ethnicity` and the requested names.

## Description

Generates random first and/or last names that are consistent with a given gender and ethnicity. Names are sampled in proportion to how often they occur in the embedded [randomNamesData](randomNamesData.html) data set, so the result looks like a realistic roster. Random names are useful to anonymise results that would otherwise identify people.

## Details

The number of names returned is the largest of `n`, `length(gender)` and `length(ethnicity)`; shorter vectors are recycled. Gender is used only for first names; ethnicity is used for both first and last names. A missing gender or ethnicity (`NA`, or not supplied) is drawn at random: gender with equal probability, ethnicity with equal probability across the six codes.

Gender and ethnicity may be given as codes or as text. Text is matched case-insensitively: `"Male"`/`"M"`, `"Female"`/`"F"`; and for ethnicity `"American Indian"`, `"Alaska"` or `"Native American"` (1); `"Asian"`, `"Hawaii"` or `"Pacific"` (2); `"Black"` or `"African"` (3); `"Hispanic"` or `"Latino"` (4); `"White"` or `"Caucasian"` (5); `"Middle Eastern"` or `"Arabic"` (6). A value that matches nothing is drawn at random, with a warning.

## Examples

``` R
randomNames()  # one name in "last, first" form

randomNames(5, which.names = "first")

randomNames(5, return.complete.data = TRUE)

test.df <- data.frame(
  GENDER = sample(0:1, 100, replace = TRUE),
  ETHNICITY = sample(1:6, 100, replace = TRUE)
)
head(randomNames(gender = test.df$GENDER, ethnicity = test.df$ETHNICITY))

ethnicities <- c("African American", "Hispanic", "Asian", "White", "Native American")
genders <- c("Female", "Male")
test.df <- data.frame(
  GENDER = sample(genders, 100, replace = TRUE),
  ETHNICITY = sample(ethnicities, 100, replace = TRUE)
)
head(randomNames(gender = test.df$GENDER, ethnicity = test.df$ETHNICITY))
```
